schema_description: openEHR Access Control: a draft change proposal for a concrete ACCESS_CONTROL_SETTINGS scheme of access directives (consent, restriction, opt-out, delegation, sensitivity labels) carried by EHR_ACCESS, and a versioned ACCESS_POLICY of a controller. The classes hold facts; the decision procedure is fixed by the scheme. Not an openEHR release.

ACCESS_DIRECTIVE_SETTINGS.name: ACCESS_DIRECTIVE_SETTINGS
ACCESS_DIRECTIVE_SETTINGS.documentation: The concrete `ACCESS_CONTROL_SETTINGS` of the access directive scheme, carried by `EHR_ACCESS._settings_` and versioned with the EHR. It records the facts an access decision about one EHR rests on: the default disposition, the gate-keepers who may change the settings, the directives the subject or their representative gave (consent, restriction, opt-out, delegation scope), and sensitivity labels on individual versioned objects. It carries no rule language: the decision procedure that reads these facts is fixed by the scheme. `EHR_ACCESS.scheme()` returns `access_directives` for an instance of this class.

default_access.name: default_access
default_access.documentation: What the EHR admits where no directive applies, coded in the `access default` group: `open` (any caller the other layers admit), `restricted` (only callers a permit directive, a gate-keeper or a care relationship names) or `consent_required` (only callers a permit directive names, apart from the subject and an emergency override).

gate_keepers.name: gate_keepers
gate_keepers.documentation: The parties who may commit a new version of the `EHR_ACCESS` that holds these settings: usually `PARTY_SELF` for a competent adult, otherwise a parent, guardian or other responsible party referenced into the demographic service (BASE Architecture Overview, Security, Access Control of access settings). Empty leaves the change to the system's administrators.

directives.name: directives
directives.documentation: The directives in force or recorded for this EHR. A directive outside its `_time_validity_` is kept as history and decides nothing.

labels.name: labels
labels.documentation: Sensitivity labels on individual versioned objects of the EHR, beside the labels the system's `ACCESS_POLICY` classification gives whole kinds of data.

scheme.name: scheme
scheme.documentation: The name of this scheme, `access_directives`, which `EHR_ACCESS.scheme()` returns.

ACCESS_DIRECTIVE.name: ACCESS_DIRECTIVE
ACCESS_DIRECTIVE.documentation: One instruction about access to the data of one EHR, given by the subject, their representative or the controller on their instruction: a consent permit or deny, an EHDS Art. 8 restriction, an EHDS Art. 10 opt-out, or the scope of a delegation. A directive applies to an access when every attribute it sets matches the access (the actor, the operation, the purpose, the data, the time), and none of its exceptions applies. Where a permit and a deny both apply, the deny wins.

kind.name: kind
kind.documentation: What kind of instruction this is, coded in the `access directive kind` group: `consent`, `restriction`, `opt_out` or `delegation`. The kind decides which callers the directive can bind and how a refusal is shown (a restriction and an opt-out read as absent).

effect.name: effect
effect.documentation: Whether the directive permits or denies the access it applies to, coded in the `access effect` group: `permit` or `deny`.

applies_to.name: applies_to
applies_to.documentation: The callers the directive applies to; any one matching scope is enough. Empty applies to every caller the kind can bind.

operations.name: operations
operations.documentation: The operations the directive applies to, coded in the operation terminology the system documents (such as `read`, `write`, `export`). Empty applies to every operation.

purposes.name: purposes
purposes.documentation: The purposes of use the directive applies to, coded in the purpose-of-use terminology the system accepts. Empty applies to every purpose.

data.name: data
data.documentation: The data the directive applies to; data in any one scope is covered. Empty applies to the whole EHR, including data recorded after the directive.

time_validity.name: time_validity
time_validity.documentation: When the directive is in force. Void is in force from the commit of the version that adds it until a later version removes it.

emergency_override.name: emergency_override
emergency_override.documentation: Whether a caller declaring an emergency purpose of use, under the system's emergency rules, is exempt from this directive (EHDS Art. 11(5) for a restriction; Art. 10(2) for an opt-out where national law allows it).

exceptions.name: exceptions
exceptions.documentation: Narrower directives of the opposite effect inside this one, such as 'deny mental health data, except to my GP'. An access an exception applies to is not decided by this directive.

instructed_by.name: instructed_by
instructed_by.documentation: Who gave the instruction: `PARTY_SELF` for the subject, otherwise their representative or the professional who recorded it on their behalf.

legal_grounds.name: legal_grounds
legal_grounds.documentation: The legal provisions the directive rests on, such as GDPR Art. 9(2)(a), EHDS Art. 8 or a national provision, coded in a terminology the jurisdiction names.

evidence.name: evidence
evidence.documentation: The record of the instruction in the EHR, such as the `ADMIN_ENTRY` that holds the signed consent (RM EHR IM, Entry package, Standard Clinical Types of Data).

identifiers.name: identifiers
identifiers.documentation: Identifiers of the directive in other systems, such as a FHIR `Consent.identifier`, an IHE BPPC or APPC policy identifier, or a national consent registry reference.

details.name: details
details.documentation: Further archetyped detail the deployment records with the directive. The decision procedure never reads it.

is_deny.name: is_deny
is_deny.documentation: True when `_effect_` is the `deny` code of the `access effect` group.

is_restriction.name: is_restriction
is_restriction.documentation: True when `_kind_` is the `restriction` code of the `access directive kind` group.

is_opt_out.name: is_opt_out
is_opt_out.documentation: True when `_kind_` is the `opt_out` code of the `access directive kind` group.

invariants.Exceptions_opposite: exceptions /= Void implies exceptions.for_all (e | e.is_deny /= is_deny and e.exceptions = Void)

ACCESS_ACTOR_SCOPE.name: ACCESS_ACTOR_SCOPE
ACCESS_ACTOR_SCOPE.documentation: A description of callers. A caller matches when it matches every attribute that is set.

party.name: party
party.documentation: A party in the demographic service: a `PERSON` or `AGENT` matches itself; an `ORGANISATION` or `GROUP` matches every caller that acts for it or is a member of it.

role.name: role
role.documentation: A functional role the caller holds, coded as the role's capability or the caller's token states it, such as a professional role code.

relationship.name: relationship
relationship.documentation: A relationship the caller must hold to the subject of the EHR, coded in the `access relationship` group: `care` (a live care relationship), `representative` or `proxy`.

caller_kind.name: caller_kind
caller_kind.documentation: The kind of caller, coded in the `access caller kind` group: `professional`, `access_service`, `subject`, `representative` or `system`.

invariants.Not_empty: party /= Void or role /= Void or relationship /= Void or caller_kind /= Void

ACCESS_DATA_SCOPE.name: ACCESS_DATA_SCOPE
ACCESS_DATA_SCOPE.documentation: A description of data in an EHR. Data match when they match every attribute that is set, and an attribute holding a list matches when any of its members does.

objects.name: objects
objects.documentation: Individual versioned objects, such as one `VERSIONED_COMPOSITION`.

templates.name: templates
templates.documentation: Template identifiers the data were committed under.

archetypes.name: archetypes
archetypes.documentation: Root archetypes of the data; a specialisation of a named archetype matches too.

categories.name: categories
categories.documentation: Categories of the data, such as the EHDS priority categories, coded in a terminology the jurisdiction names.

sensitivities.name: sensitivities
sensitivities.documentation: Sensitivity codes, matched against the labels the data carry, coded in a terminology the system documents (such as the HL7 v3 confidentiality and sensitivity codes).

origins.name: origins
origins.documentation: The systems the data came from, as `FEEDER_AUDIT_DETAILS._system_id_` or the committing system's `_system_id_` records them.

invariants.Not_empty: objects /= Void or templates /= Void or archetypes /= Void or categories /= Void or sensitivities /= Void or origins /= Void or recorded /= Void

ACCESS_LABEL.name: ACCESS_LABEL
ACCESS_LABEL.documentation: Sensitivity labels on one versioned object of the EHR. A caller reads labelled data only when a capability clears every label, a permit directive names the label, or an emergency override applies.

target.name: target
target.documentation: The versioned object the labels apply to.

sensitivities.name: sensitivities
sensitivities.documentation: The sensitivity codes the object carries.

reason.name: reason
reason.documentation: Why the object is labelled, never clinical content.

ACCESS_POLICY.name: ACCESS_POLICY
ACCESS_POLICY.documentation: The access policy of a system or of one controller in it: facts that hold for every EHR the controller keeps. It classifies kinds of data into sensitivities, states whether clinical access needs a care relationship and a declared purpose, lists the named directives a subject can accept by reference, and states what the subject's view of the access log withholds. Kept in its own versioned container, outside any EHR and outside the demographic service.

controller.name: controller
controller.documentation: The `ORGANISATION` whose policy this is, the controller of the data.

classifications.name: classifications
classifications.documentation: The rules that give kinds of data their sensitivity labels.

care_relationship_required.name: care_relationship_required
care_relationship_required.documentation: Whether a professional's clinical access to an EHR needs a live care relationship to its subject, beyond the operation the caller's capability grants.

relationship_grace.name: relationship_grace
relationship_grace.documentation: How long after a care relationship ends it still admits access, for follow-up (BASE Architecture Overview, Security, Time-limitation of access).

purpose_required.name: purpose_required
purpose_required.documentation: Whether an access to clinical data must declare a purpose of use.

catalogue.name: catalogue
catalogue.documentation: Named directives a subject can accept by an identifier, such as an IHE BPPC policy or a national consent choice. Each carries at least one identifier.

log_restrictions.name: log_restrictions
log_restrictions.documentation: The restrictions a Member State law lays on the subject's view of the access log under EHDS Article 9(3). Each names the kinds of accessor and the attributes of the accessor the subject view withholds; the full entry is unchanged.

details.name: details
details.documentation: Further archetyped detail. The decision procedure never reads it.

invariants.Catalogue_identified: catalogue /= Void implies catalogue.for_all (d | d.identifiers /= Void)

ACCESS_CLASSIFICATION.name: ACCESS_CLASSIFICATION
ACCESS_CLASSIFICATION.documentation: One classification rule: data the scope describes carry the given sensitivity labels.

data.name: data
data.documentation: The kind of data the rule classifies. It names no individual object.

sensitivities.name: sensitivities
sensitivities.documentation: The sensitivity codes the data carry.

ACCESS_LOG_RESTRICTION.name: ACCESS_LOG_RESTRICTION
ACCESS_LOG_RESTRICTION.documentation: One restriction of the subject's view of the access log under EHDS Article 9(3). The entries whose accessor is of one of the given kinds are shown to the subject and their representative without the given attributes of the accessor; a reviewer reads the full entry.

accessor_kinds.name: accessor_kinds
accessor_kinds.documentation: The kinds of accessor the restriction applies to, coded in the openEHR Terminology `accessor kind` group of the access log, which `ACCESSOR._kind_` is coded in.

withheld.name: withheld
withheld.documentation: The attributes of `ACCESSOR` the subject view withholds, coded in the `access log withheld` group: `accessor_party`, `accessor_provider`, `accessor_roles` or `accessor_groups`.

legal_grounds.name: legal_grounds
legal_grounds.documentation: The provisions of the Member State law that lay the restriction down under EHDS Article 9(3), coded in a terminology the jurisdiction names.

VERSIONED_ACCESS_POLICY.name: VERSIONED_ACCESS_POLICY
VERSIONED_ACCESS_POLICY.documentation: Version container for an `ACCESS_POLICY`, committed in contributions with their audit like any other versioned object.
